欽定協紀辨方書 · 1741

The Court Almanac: What a Day Suits and What It Avoids

In 1741 the Qianlong court published 欽定協紀辨方書 to settle the almanac's 宜 (suits) and 忌 (avoid), which the printed almanacs had muddled. This page works out a day exactly by its rules and shows which rule decided each line. It is a calendar custom, not a forecast.

A day

Choose a date

Any date from 1900 to 2100. Worked out on the Beijing calendar, as the book was: the month opens on the day of its 節, the lunar date follows the new moon at Beijing.

Worked out on this device. Nothing is sent to us.

The method, in the book's words

The title means keeping heaven's order and earth's directions:

「夫協紀辨方者敬天之紀敬地之方也」

Each day has one of twelve officers, counted from the month's own branch:

「厯家以建除滿平定執破危成收開閉凡十二日周而復始」

Activities are the warp and spirits the weft:

「鋪註萬年書則以事為經以神為緯」

When good and ruling-out spirits share a day, the book weighs them in six grades, from the top one:

「其上吉足勝凶從宜不從忌」

Quoted as printed: 欽定協紀辨方書, 四庫全書 edition, public domain on Chinese Wikisource.

      What this page leaves out, and why

      Healing (療病), ground-breaking for graves (破土), burial (安葬) and reburial (啟攢): the book lists them, but Fate Tutor does not give advice on health or funerals. They are worked out by the engine and checked, but not shown.

      Hours (卷三十二), directions and the year's spirits by compass point (卷三, 卷十四 to 卷十九): this page is about the day.

      Marriage matching by birth year (合婚): the book itself throws it out as groundless, and so does this site.

      The online copy leaves the month tables' day-by-day 宜 and 忌 blank, so the page works each day out from the book's rules instead, and the checker tests those rules against everything the copy does print.

      Where this comes from

      欽定協紀辨方書, 四庫全書 edition

      Compiled by order of the Qianlong emperor under 允祿, 梅瑴成 and 何國宗 and finished in 1741; all 36 volumes, public domain on Chinese Wikisource. Spirits' places come from volumes 4 to 9, the 宜 and 忌 from volumes 10 and 11.

      Checked: every spirit's place against its rule sentence (51,060 places), the month tables' notes and 711 day headings, the editors' 64 statements of which spirits share a day, and volume 10 against volume 11. Where the editors correct an older rule (天願, 地囊, 天火 and others), their correction is used and named.

      About this tradition

      Choosing the day

      Choosing a day (擇日) is one of the oldest customs of the Chinese calendar. The Qing court found the almanacs in use full of copying slips and contradictions, and had this book compiled to set one rule for the imperial almanac.

      Fate Tutor sets out the book's rules and shows its sources. It does not turn them into a forecast, financial advice, medical advice or a decision made for you.

      These are traditional systems of belief. They are not science and they do not predict the future. Fate Tutor shows what each tradition says and where it says it, in the language of tendencies.
